newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Fujimori seeks freedom for jailed general.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Fujimori seeks freedom for jailed general.

text.p: Peru's President Alberto Fujimori proposed late on Tuesday an amnesty law for retired officers under trial for criticising the military that would allow the release of a general jailed amid controversy last week.

The military's detention of Gen. Rodolfo Robles for "insubordination" after he blamed the army for recently bombing a local television station has provoked a political storm in Peru and brought a public campaign to free him.

Fujimori's bill, expected to be passed on Thursday by the government-controlled Congress, would extend an amnesty to all retired officers and leave the military vulnerable to criticism from more of its former members.
"This is a triumph for the people," said Francisco Soberon, director of Aprodeh, one of several local human rights groups to allege the military is guilty of widespread abuses.
Robles, now likely to be freed by the weekend, has frequently spoken out against Peru's military.

After claiming an army "death squad" killed 10 students and a university teacher in 1992, he went into exile in Argentina to avoid trial but later returned to Peru when the government granted him amnesty.
